lesson.subtitle: Lesson 4 -- What Is Happening Right Now
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Viviane Rodrigues de Oliveira | Lesson 4 -- What Is Happening Right Now

listenings.text: Morning everyone, quick update from my side. We are running three things in parallel this month, so I will be short. First, the training. We are training the store managers and we are almost done, thirty-one out of forty-one. Second, the systems. We are still working with two systems at the same time, because the new one is not ready, and honestly it is costing us about six hours a week. I am not happy about that. Third, the job titles. We are not moving there, we are waiting for the model from headquarters. So that is my only real blocker. One good thing before I stop: people are asking a lot more questions than before, and they are asking them in the meetings and not in the corridor. For me that is the best sign we have.

There is one question I ask in every first interview, and candidates almost never prepare it. What are you working on right now? It sounds like small talk. It is not. I ask it because I want to hear if you are close to the work or far from it. When somebody answers with the job description, I learn nothing. When somebody says I am training forty store managers this month and we are at thirty-one, I know exactly who I am talking to. Two small things. Use the continuous, because right now is not the same as always. And say one thing that is not going well. Candidates who tell me only good news sound like a presentation, not like a person. The one who says this part is blocked and here is what I am doing about it, that is the one I call back.

extra_audio.text: Hello, Marco. Here is the update. Right now I am leading the culture workstream. We are training the store managers and we are at thirty-one of forty-one. We are not closing the job titles, because we are waiting for Milan.

paras: The people integration is ongoing and, in general, it is going well. We are working on four workstreams: job titles, benefits, systems and culture. I am leading the culture workstream and I am supporting the benefits one.
This month we are training the store managers on the new performance process. Forty-one managers are in the programme and thirty-one are already trained. We are finishing the last group next week.

Two things are not moving. We are not closing the job titles, because we are still waiting for the Milan model. And the new HR system is not ready, so we are working with two systems at the same time. That is costing my team about six hours a week.
One good surprise. People are asking many more questions than before, and they are asking them in the catch-up meetings and not in the corridor. That is exactly what we wanted.
